papers.title: Critical edges and endpoint sparse dominations for the lacunary spherical maximal operator
papers.abstract: We study sparse bounds for the lacunary spherical maximal operator in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. Lacey in 2019 established $(r,s)$-sparse bounds in the interior of the triangle with vertices $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, and $(\frac{d}{d+1},\frac{d}{d+1})$ in the $(1/r,1/s)$-plane. We extend these bounds to the two open critical edges, answering a question of Roos and Seeger. At their common vertex, we also obtain a sparse bound with a logarithmic modification in the first average. The main ingredient in our argument is a local estimate based on the local density of the input level sets, which replaces the modulus of continuity estimate used in Lacey's proof.

papers.title: Polynomial Spaces Are Locally Paley-Wiener: Bulk Universality and Christoffel Asymptotics on Symmetric Convex Bodies
papers.abstract: We prove a bulk universality limit for total-degree polynomial spaces on symmetric convex bodies. For a Bernstein-Markov measure with a positive continuous density near an interior point, the rescaled reproducing kernel converges to the Fourier integral over the dual unit ball of the Baran metric, which we call the local spectral body. After diagonal normalization, the limit is the Fourier transform of the uniform probability measure on this body. The result holds uniformly on compact subsets where the local density assumption holds and yields the corresponding Christoffel asymptotic. Its main constructive ingredient is recovery, with the exact rescaled $L^2$ norm, of Paley-Wiener functions at arbitrary interior centres by Chebyshev ridge polynomials. This extends the classical polynomial-entire function limit at the symmetry centre to a position-dependent local spectrum. Ellipsoidal spectral bodies recover the known Bessel profile on the ball; polytopal spectral bodies give other Fourier profiles. For rectangles, the two-dimensional profile is a product of two sinc functions. On a regular hexagon, the local spectral body changes from a hexagon to a parallelogram across the inscribed circle; explicit Fourier profiles are available in both regimes. The proof uses the Siciak extremal function and does not require a differential operator or an explicit orthogonal-polynomial kernel.

papers.title: A One-Sided Liouville Theorem and a Critical Sparse-Support Inverse Theorem for Discrete Harmonic Functions
papers.abstract: We answer the one-sided Liouville question of Buhovsky, Logunov, Malinnikova, and Sodin (Duke Math. J. 171 (2022), Remark 1.4). There is an absolute $\varepsilon>0$ such that a real harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is constant if it is nonnegative on at least a $1-\varepsilon$ proportion of every sufficiently large centered square. More generally, for every nonconstant real harmonic function and every $a\le b$, the sets $\{u<a\}$ and $\{u>b\}$ each occupy a fixed positive proportion of the same arbitrarily large centered squares. Turning from sign conditions to sparse supports, we prove in three dimensions a local inverse theorem at the critical quadratic support scale. Write $Q_R=[-R,R]^3\cap\mathbb{Z}^3$. If a complex-valued function is harmonic in $Q_{30R}$ and has at most $AR^2$ nonzero values there, its support in $Q_R$ lies in at most $K_A$ characteristic planes $x_i\pm x_j=c$. The minimum number $m_3(N)$ of nonzero values in $Q_N$ among whole-lattice harmonic functions nonzero at the origin satisfies $m_3(N)=(1+o(1))(2N+1)^2$. More generally, if a fixed nonzero harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ has $O(N^2)$ nonzero values in $Q_N$ along a sequence $N\to\infty$, then its support has a unique irredundant cover by finitely many characteristic planes. If there are $k$ such planes, the support count in $Q_N$ is $k(2N+1)^2+O_u(N)$.

papers.title: Multiple Positive Solutions of Minkowski-Curvature Neumann Problems with a Two-Step Indefinite Weight
papers.abstract: We study positive solutions of the Minkowski-curvature Neumann problem \[ \left(\frac{u'}{\sqrt{1-(u')^2}}\right)' + a(t)g(u)=0,\qquad u'(0)=u'(T)=0, \] with a two-step sign-changing weight. Under an explicit condition on an increasing nonlinearity \(g\), we prove that for every prescribed integer \(N\ge 1\) and every prescribed ratio \(\kappa>0\) of the step lengths, there exist step weights of that ratio and strictly negative integral for which the problem has at least \(N\) distinct positive solutions. The multiplicity persists under small perturbations of the weight parameters. A structural condition on \(g'/g\) yields at least three positive Neumann solutions for \(g(u)=e^{u^p}-1\) for every \(p>1\). An explicit increasing nonlinearity also satisfies the \(N\)-solution criterion for every finite \(N\), with the weight chosen separately in each case.

papers.title: Oscillatory integral operators of arbitrary signature: beyond the universal estimates
papers.abstract: We consider H\"ormander oscillatory integral operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$. In particular, we are interested in proving bounds with dependence on the signature of the phase. The sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^p$ estimates was obtained for any given signature by the second author and Iliopoulou. Under the mild non-compression hypotheses on the phase introduced in Chen et al., we prove $L^p\to L^p$ estimates that go beyond this universal range in odd dimensions. We also obtain the sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^q$ estimates for odd $n$. The techniques are based on the breakthrough work of Wang--Wu on the Fourier restriction conjecture.

papers.title: Nonlinear Fourier series
papers.abstract: We survey aspects of nonlinear Fourier series as presented in the 2026 Brouwer lecture by the second author. The fast nonlinear Fourier expansion mentioned in the lecture is further elaborated in joint work with the first author.

papers.title: Amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves and applications
papers.abstract: We prove amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves in arbitrary dimensions. The proof uses the sharp square function estimates of Maldague and Guth-Maldague. As an application, we establish sharp small cap decoupling inequalities for the moment curve in every dimension $n\geq4$. This proves the conjecture of Demeter-Guth-Wang on exponential sums in all dimensions.
